newsitem.title: USA: Qwest leases New York-Washington link from Amtrak.
newsitem.headline: Qwest leases New York-Washington link from Amtrak.

text.p: Qwest Communications Corp has agreed to lease access to the Northeast Corridor right of way for the New York-to-Washington link of its nationwide fiber optic communications network, Amtrak said Tuesday.
The lease will generate significant revenue for Amtrak, its statement said.
Spokesman Rick Remington said Qwest had requested that the amount be removed from the statement.
Qwest spokesman Tony Brodman declined to elaborate.

Amtrak said the lease would enable Qwest to use an existing duct system running underneath the Northeast Corridor rail line to install fiber optic cables, as well as space along the railroad right of way to build support facilities.
Qwest was founded in 1988 as SP Telecom, a Southern Pacific subsidiary, which gave it access to that railroad's right of way -- now part of the Union Pacific system.
Brodman said Qwest's planned 14,000 route mile system was about 40 per cent complete.
